title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 2 An action brought for infringement of a patent right shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the place where the infringing act is committed or of the place where the defendant has his domicile.
The place of infringing act includes: the place where the manufacture, use, offer for sale, sale, import, and other acts of the product accused of infringing an invention or utility model patent right are committed; the place where the use of a patented method is committed; the place where the use, offer for sale, sale, import, and other acts of the product directly obtained in accordance with the patented method are committed; the place where the manufacture, offer for sale, sale, import, and other acts of a design patent product are committed; and the place where the act of counterfeiting another person's patent is committed. The place where the infringing results occur as a result of the above-mentioned infringing acts likewise falls within the place where the infringing act is committed.

Article 3 Where the plaintiff only brings an action against the manufacturer of the infringing product and does not bring an action against the seller, and the place of manufacture of the infringing product is different from the place of sale, the People's Court of the place of manufacture shall have jurisdiction; where the action is brought with both the manufacturer and the seller as co-defendants, the People's Court of the place of sale shall have jurisdiction.
Where the seller is a branch of the manufacturer, and the plaintiff brings an action in the place of sale against the manufacturer for its manufacturing and selling acts, the People's Court of the place of sale shall have jurisdiction.

Article 4 For an action for patent infringement brought against a utility model patent with a filing date before October 1, 2009 (excluding that day), the plaintiff may submit a search report produced by the patent administrative department of the State Council; for an action for patent infringement brought against a utility model patent or design patent with a filing date on or after October 1, 2009, the plaintiff may submit a patent evaluation report produced by the patent administrative department of the State Council. Where necessary for the trial of the case, the People's Court may require the plaintiff to submit a search report or a patent evaluation report. If the plaintiff fails to submit it without justifiable reasons, the People's Court may rule to suspend the action or order the plaintiff to bear the possible adverse consequences.
Where the defendant in a case involving infringement of a utility model or design patent right requests suspension of the action, it shall, within the defence period, file a request for invalidation of the plaintiff's patent right.

Article 6 In a case involving infringement of a utility model or design patent right accepted by the People's Court, if the defendant requests a declaration of invalidity of the patent right after the expiry of the defence period, the People's Court shall not suspend the action, except where it considers, upon examination, that it is necessary to suspend the action.

Article 7 In a case involving infringement of an invention patent right accepted by the People's Court, or a case involving infringement of a utility model or design patent right in which the patent right has been maintained upon examination by the patent administrative department of the State Council, if the defendant requests a declaration of invalidity of the patent right within the defence period, the People's Court may not suspend the action.

Article 8 Where the People's Court decides to suspend the action, and the patentee or an interested party requests the court to order the defendant to stop the relevant acts or take other measures to prevent the continuing expansion of infringing damage, and provides a guarantee, the People's Court may, upon examination, if it finds that the request conforms to the relevant legal provisions, make a relevant ruling at the same time as it rules to suspend the action.

Article 9 Where the People's Court takes property preservation measures against a patent right, it shall issue a notice of assistance in enforcement to the patent administrative department of the State Council, stating the matters requiring assistance in enforcement and the period for preservation of the patent right, and attach the ruling made by the People's Court.
The period for preservation of a patent right shall not exceed six months at a time, calculated from the date on which the patent administrative department of the State Council receives the notice of assistance in enforcement. If it is still necessary to continue the preservation measures against the patent right, the People's Court shall, before the expiry of the preservation period, deliver separately to the patent administrative department of the State Council a notice of assistance in enforcement for continued preservation. If the notice is not delivered before the expiry of the preservation period, the property preservation against the patent right shall be deemed to have been automatically lifted.
The People's Court may take property preservation measures against a pledged patent right, and the right of the pledgee to be repaid on a priority basis shall not be affected by the preservation measures; an exclusive implementation license contract already concluded between the patentee and the licensee shall not affect the property preservation of the patent right by the People's Court.
The People's Court shall not repeatedly preserve a patent right that has already been preserved.

Article 10 Where an invention-creation completed before July 1, 2001 by utilizing the material and technical conditions of the entity has a contract between the entity and the inventor or designer stipulating the ownership of the right to apply for a patent and the patent right, that stipulation shall prevail.

Article 11 In a case involving infringement of a patent right accepted by the People's Court, where a conflict of rights is involved, the lawful rights and interests of a party who enjoys the rights in accordance with the law at an earlier time shall be protected.

Article 12 The lawful rights referred to in paragraph 3 of Article 23 of the Patent Law include lawful rights or interests enjoyed in respect of works, trademarks, geographical indications, names, enterprise names, portraits, as well as commodity names, packaging, and decoration that have a certain influence.

Article 13 The phrase 'the scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent right shall be determined by the contents of the claims, and the description and appended drawings may be used to explain the contents of the claims' in paragraph 1 of Article 59 of the Patent Law means that the scope of protection of the patent right shall be determined by the scope defined by all the technical features recorded in the claims, and shall also include the scope defined by features equivalent to the said technical features.
Equivalent features refer to features that, compared with the recorded technical features, are identical in the basic means, perform the same basic function, and achieve the same basic effect, and which a person of ordinary skill in the art would have been able to conceive of without any creative effort at the time of the occurrence of the alleged infringing act.

Article 14 The actual losses suffered by the right holder as a result of the infringement as provided in Article 65 of the Patent Law may be calculated as the product of the total decrease in the sales volume of the patentee's patented products caused by the infringement multiplied by the reasonable profit per patented product. Where the total decrease in the sales volume of the right holder is difficult to determine, the product of the total sales volume of the infringing products on the market multiplied by the reasonable profit per patented product may be deemed to be the actual losses suffered by the right holder as a result of the infringement.
The benefits obtained by the infringer from the infringement as provided in Article 65 of the Patent Law may be calculated as the product of the total sales volume of the infringing products on the market multiplied by the reasonable profit per infringing product. The benefits obtained by the infringer from the infringement shall generally be calculated according to the operating profit of the infringer; for an infringer who is wholly engaged in infringement, the benefits may be calculated according to the sales profit.

Article 15 Where the losses of the right holder or the benefits obtained by the infringer are difficult to determine, and there is a patent license fee that can be referred to, the People's Court may, in view of the type of the patent right, the nature and circumstances of the infringing act, the nature, scope, time and other factors of the patent license, reasonably determine the amount of damages by reference to a multiple of the patent license fee; where there is no patent license fee that can be referred to, or the patent license fee is obviously unreasonable, the People's Court may determine the amount of damages in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 65 of the Patent Law, taking into account the type of the patent right, the nature and circumstances of the infringing act and other factors.

Article 16 Where the right holder claims that it has paid reasonable expenses for stopping the infringing act, the People's Court may calculate such expenses separately in addition to the amount of compensation determined in accordance with Article 65 of the Patent Law.

Article 17 The limitation of action for infringement of a patent right shall be three years, calculated from the date on which the patentee or an interested party knows or should have known of the damage to the right and of the obligor. Where the right holder brings a prosecution after more than three years, if the infringing act is still continuing at the time of the prosecution, and the patent right is still within its validity period, the People's Court shall order the defendant to stop the infringing act, and the amount of damages for the infringement shall be calculated retroactively for three years from the date on which the right holder brought the prosecution in the People's Court.

Article 18 The offer for sale referred to in Articles 11 and 69 of the Patent Law means an expression of intention to sell a commodity by means such as advertising, displaying it in a shop window, or exhibiting it at a trade fair.

Article 19 In a case involving infringement of a patent right accepted by the People's Court, if the department administering patent work has already made a determination of infringement or non-infringement, the People's Court shall still conduct a comprehensive examination of the parties' litigation claims.
Article 20 Where any previous relevant judicial interpretations are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
